get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Never touches the database.
Readiness: the API can serve real requests. 503 while the database is down.

post.description: Web: log in and receive the session in an HttpOnly cookie.
Mobile: log in and receive the token, for `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
End this session and clear its cookies.

get.description: Your logged-in devices, most recently used first.

schema.title: Response Sessions Api Auth Sessions Get

delete.description: Log a device out. Revoking the current session also clears its cookies.

get.description: The whole tree, flat, each category with its child and part counts.

schema.title: Response List Categories Api Catalog Categories Get

post.description: A new category, at the root when no parent is named.

patch.description: Rename a category, move it, set its tracking, or a mix. A no-op changes nothing.

delete.description: Deletes the category and its own attribute definitions. Refuses one still in use.

get.description: Every field the category's parts have, inherited ones marked.

post.description: A new field on the category. A key an ancestor already defines is refused.

patch.description: Label, required, options and position. No stored part value is touched.

delete.description: Removes the definition. The values stay, and their parts are flagged on read.

get.description: A page of parts, narrowed by a name substring and by category.

post.description: A new part, with every value validated against its category's resolved schema.

get.description: One part. A part whose values no longer fit is returned, marked for review.

patch.description: Replaces the details and the whole attribute map, so nothing is saved half-valid.

get.description: The pins in their saved order. A part with none answers an empty list, not 404.

put.description: The whole table at once, so no pinout is ever stored half-saved. No pins clears it.

post.description: A page of the parts the search matches, ordered and continued from its cursor.

get.description: What the category's parts hold, counted over text and pin only (requirement 5.2).
A part's attachments, newest first (requirement 1.6).

schema.title: Response List Attachments Api Files Attachments Get

post.description: Store an upload's bytes and attach them to a part (requirements 1.1, 1.3-1.5).

get.description: The bytes, streamed with their type and title; `?download=1` sends a download (3).

patch.description: Rename or re-kind an attachment (requirement 4.1). A no-op edit writes nothing.

delete.description: Remove the attachment; its file goes when nothing else uses it (requirement 4.2).

get.description: The whole tree, flat, each location with its child and lot counts.

schema.title: Response List Locations Api Inventory Locations Get

post.description: A new location, at the root when no parent is named, its short code minted.

patch.description: Rename a location, move it, or both. A no-op changes nothing; the code is kept.

delete.description: Deletes an empty location. Refuses one that has children or holds lots (1.10).

post.description: Append a RECEIVE into (part, location) and answer the lot's new balance.
Recount a lot to an absolute counted quantity and answer its new balance.
Move a quantity between two locations and answer both lots' balances.

get.description: The total on_hand for each part asked about; a part with none is simply absent.

schema.title: Response Parts Stock Api Inventory Parts Stock Get

get.description: One part's total and its per-location breakdown; zero and empty when never held.
Units matching a code/serial/MAC substring, each with its location (6.3, 2.5).

schema.title: Response Search Units Api Inventory Units Get

post.description: Receive N units of a unit-tracked part; answer the units and the lot's balance.

get.description: The part's units, each with code, serial, MAC, status and location (6.1).

schema.title: Response Units Of Part Api Inventory Parts  Part Id  Units Get

get.description: The units sitting in the location, across every lot there (requirement 6.2).

schema.title: Response Units Of Location Api Inventory Locations  Location Id  Units Get

get.description: One unit, or 404 for one this workspace doesn't hold (requirement 7.2).

patch.description: Set a unit's serial and MAC, refusing a duplicate; a no-op changes nothing (5.6).

delete.description: Delete a retired unit; an in-stock one is a 409 (requirement 6.4).

post.description: Move a unit to a destination location, 422 if retired or already there (4.4, 4.5).
Retire a unit, writing the compensating ADJUST -1; a retired unit is a no-op (3.1).
Un-retire a unit, writing the compensating ADJUST +1; in-stock is a no-op (3.2).

Define a part and receive its first stock in one transaction (requirement 1).

422 with every problem at once, 409 naming the part that holds the manufacturer and
part number, 404 for a duplicate's source the workspace doesn't hold (3.4).

What every row of the sheet will do, writing nothing (requirement 7).

A plan with problems is still a 200: finding them is what a preview is for (7.5).
Only a sheet that can't be read at all is a 422, with its code and column (4.6).

Import the sheet its preview showed, all in one transaction (requirement 8).

422 with the problems when the plan has any, 409 when the outcome changed since the
preview's digest; either way nothing is written (8.2, 8.3).

get.description:
The header row of the nine fixed columns, as a CSV download (requirement 4.9).

Reads no workspace, but only a signed-in caller gets it, as every other read.

post.description: A new draft, labelled as given or suggested; 409 for a label taken (4.1, 4.3).

patch.description: Replaces the label, summary and notes whole, in any status (requirement 4.8).

delete.description: A draft revision of a project that keeps another; 409 otherwise (5.1 to 5.3).

post.description: A draft of the same project started from this one, whatever its status (6.1).

get.description:
The lines oldest first, the shortage report as stock stands now, and whether the
BOM can change (requirements 4.11, 5.2, 6.1, 6.7).

post.description:
A line after the others; 409 for a designator another line holds, or a revision
that isn't a draft (requirements 4.1, 4.6, 5.1).

patch.description:
Replaces the line's part, designators, quantity and notes whole; a no-op writes
nothing (requirement 4.9).

delete.description: The line and its designators, while the revision is a draft (4.10, 5.1).

get.description:
The projects, newest activity first, narrowed by a text in the name and by tags
they all carry, each tag normalized as a stored one is (3.1 to 3.5).

schema.title: Response List Projects Api Projects Get

post.description: A new project with its revision A; 409 for a name another project holds (1.1, 1.3).

get.description: Each tag the workspace's projects carry, with its count, alphabetical (2.6).

schema.title: Response List Project Tags Api Projects Tags Get

get.description: A project page: its revisions, the latest and the next label (requirement 1.6).

patch.description: Replaces the name, description and tags whole; a no-op writes nothing (1.5).

delete.description: The project and its revisions; 409 while one of them isn't a draft (1.7, 1.8).

AdjustRequest.title: AdjustRequest
AdjustRequest.description:
Recounting a lot to an absolute counted quantity, with a reason (4.3, 4.4).

`counted` is the absolute number the owner counted, not a delta: the use case works out
the signed change and stores that.

AttachmentResponse.title: AttachmentResponse
AttachmentResponse.description:
One attachment as a part page shows it, with the link its content is read from.

`subject` travels as the `part:<uuid>` string it parses from, so the web sends it back
unchanged when it lists or uploads. `size` is the file's byte count and `media_type` its
sniffed type; `content_url` is the API path the bytes are streamed from (design §6).

AttributeProblemResponse.title: AttributeProblemResponse
AttributeProblemResponse.description: One attribute of a part that no longer fits its schema (requirement 5.3).

AttributeValueResponse.title: AttributeValueResponse
AttributeValueResponse.description:
One stored value, in the three forms the web needs (requirements 3.9, 3.10).

`value` is the exact stored value, a string for a number because JSON numbers are
doubles in every client we generate and exactness is the whole point. `display` is the
same number in engineering notation, so 4700 reads as `4.7k`, and `unit` labels it.

BalanceResponse.title: BalanceResponse
BalanceResponse.description:
The resulting balance a movement answers with, so the web updates in place.

`available` is `on_hand - reserved`; in v0.4.0 `reserved` is always zero, so it equals
`on_hand`, but the field is here from day one (design's HTTP API, requirement 3.4).

BomLineRequest.title: BomLineRequest
BomLineRequest.description:
A line to add, or the whole of a line being edited (requirement 4.9).

The designators are a list as typed, `r1-4, R7`; blank text is none. The quantity may be
left out when there are designators, since their count is the quantity (decision 7).

BomLineResponse.title: BomLineResponse
BomLineResponse.description: A line, its designators both as a list and as canonical text (requirement 4.11).

BomPartFactsResponse.title: BomPartFactsResponse
BomPartFactsResponse.description: What the catalog says about a part on the BOM, as it stands at this read (8.3).

BomPartResponse.title: BomPartResponse
BomPartResponse.description:
One part of the report (requirement 6.1). An unknown part has no facts; it and a
consumable have no available stock and are never short (6.4, 6.5).

BomRefusalResponse.title: BomRefusalResponse
BomRefusalResponse.description:
The `detail` of a refused line write (design's Error Handling).

The sentence stays English; the code is what the web translates, and the field is where
the editor shows it. `item` names the designator or the typed item refused; a designator
another line holds also names that line, by id and canonical text.

BomResponse.title: BomResponse
BomResponse.description:
A revision's BOM: its lines oldest first, its report, and whether it can change,
which only a draft's can (requirement 5.2).

BoolCountsResponse.title: BoolCountsResponse
BoolCountsResponse.description: How many parts hold true and how many hold false for a boolean attribute.

BoolFilterRequest.title: BoolFilterRequest
BoolFilterRequest.description: A boolean attribute set to true or false (requirement 2.4).

CategoryNodeResponse.title: CategoryNodeResponse
CategoryNodeResponse.description: A category as the tree shows it, with the counts requirement 1.11 asks for.

CategoryResponse.title: CategoryResponse
CategoryResponse.description:
A category on the wire. `tracked_individually` and `not_stocked` are the flags the
owner set on this category, `null` when it inherits; the `_resolved` pair are the answers
along the chain the web shows and inventory reads (requirements 6.1, 6.2; 09's 1.4).

CategorySchemaResponse.title: CategorySchemaResponse
CategorySchemaResponse.description: Every field a category's parts have, its ancestors' included (requirement 2.7).

CellProblemResponse.title: CellProblemResponse
CellProblemResponse.description:
One thing wrong, where it is, and a code the web translates (requirement 7.6).

`row` is null for a quick-add and for the sheet as a whole; `column` is a fixed column's
name or an attribute key, and null for a whole row. The message is English and safe to
show as the detail of a refused value.

ChangeAttachmentRequest.title: ChangeAttachmentRequest
ChangeAttachmentRequest.description:
A rename, a re-kind, or both. What the body left out is left alone (requirement 4.1).

The domain owns the rules: a title is trimmed and capped, a kind is one of the four, so
the value objects validate here and a bad one is the router's 422. Both left out is a
patch that carries nothing, which the use case treats as a no-op — nothing to commit.

CreateProjectRequest.title: CreateProjectRequest
CreateProjectRequest.description: A new project. Its revision A comes with it (design decision 2).

CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse
CurrentUserResponse.description: The account, plus the workspace this session acts in (ADR 0007).

EnumCountResponse.title: EnumCountResponse
EnumCountResponse.description: One enum option and how many parts have it (requirement 5.1).

FacetsResponse.title: FacetsResponse
FacetsResponse.description:
What a category's parts actually hold, per attribute of its resolved schema.

`enums[key]` is each option with its count, `bools[key]` the true/false counts,
`numbers[key]` the range some part covers or `None` when no part has a value
(requirement 5.3). Keyed by the attribute key so the web lines each facet up with the
filter it belongs to.

ImportPreviewResponse.title: ImportPreviewResponse
ImportPreviewResponse.description:
A preview's plan, problems included, since finding them is what a preview is for
(requirements 7.2-7.5). `problems` are the sheet's own; each row carries its own. The
import sends `digest` back.

ImportRequest.title: ImportRequest
ImportRequest.description:
The previewed sheet sent back with the digest its preview answered, so the import
refuses a sheet whose outcome changed since (requirement 8.3).

ImportResultResponse.title: ImportResultResponse
ImportResultResponse.description:
What an import did (requirement 8.5): the summary, the parts it defined with their
rows, and the units it received, each with its minted code and location.

ImportRowResponse.title: ImportRowResponse
ImportRowResponse.description:
One planned row: its number as the spreadsheet shows it, the part, the stock (null
for none) and every problem found in it (requirement 7.2).

ImportSheetRequest.title: ImportSheetRequest
ImportSheetRequest.description:
A sheet's text, for a preview. The characters are capped here, before it is read
(design's Limits); the entries and columns are the reader's to count.

ImportedPartResponse.title: ImportedPartResponse
ImportedPartResponse.description: A part an import defined, and the row that defined it (requirement 8.5).

LocationNodeResponse.title: LocationNodeResponse
LocationNodeResponse.description: A location as the tree shows it, with the counts requirement 1.12 asks for.

LocationResponse.title: LocationResponse
LocationResponse.description: A location on the wire, its short code shown so a bin reads as `WX-L-0007` (2.1).

LotBalanceResponse.title: LotBalanceResponse
LotBalanceResponse.description: One row of a part's per-location breakdown: where, and how much sits there (7.3).

MoveRequest.title: MoveRequest
MoveRequest.description: Moving a positive quantity of a part from one location to another (requirement 4.5).

MoveResponse.title: MoveResponse
MoveResponse.description:
Both lots' balances after a move: what left the source, and what the destination now
holds (design's HTTP API).

MoveUnitRequest.title: MoveUnitRequest
MoveUnitRequest.description: Moving one unit to a destination location (requirement 4.1).

NewRevisionRequest.title: NewRevisionRequest
NewRevisionRequest.description: A revision to add or fork. No label takes the suggested one (decision 4).

NewUnitBody.title: NewUnitBody

NumberBoundResponse.title: NumberBoundResponse
NumberBoundResponse.description:
One end of a number facet: the exact stored value and its engineering notation.

A string, not a JSON number, for the reason `AttributeValueResponse.value` is: JSON
numbers are doubles in every client we generate, and a facet bound is exact. `display`
carries no unit, as a part value's does not: the unit is the attribute's, and the web
reads it from the schema it already has, so `4700` reads as `4.7k`.

NumberRangeResponse.title: NumberRangeResponse
NumberRangeResponse.description: The lowest and highest value some part holds for a number attribute (requirement 5.1).

OptionsFilterRequest.title: OptionsFilterRequest
OptionsFilterRequest.description: One or more enum options; a part matching any of them is in (requirement 2.3).

PartOutcomeResponse.title: PartOutcomeResponse
PartOutcomeResponse.description:
What a row does with a part (requirement 7.2).

`new` carries the name and category path the row gives, `existing` the stored part's id
and name, and `same_as_row` the earlier row defining the part, with that row's name and
category. What a kind doesn't have is null.

PartPageResponse.title: PartPageResponse
PartPageResponse.description: One window of the list and the cursor the next one starts from (requirement 4.11).

PartResponse.title: PartResponse
PartResponse.description:
One part with its values, and whatever no longer fits its schema (requirement 5.2).

A value stored under a key nothing defines any more is still here, with no unit: it is
listed as a problem, never dropped (design §2.5).

PartSearchRequest.title: PartSearchRequest
PartSearchRequest.description:
One search: text, a category and its subtree, a pin, typed filters, a sort, a page.

Everything the web keeps in the address, as one body (design's Web). `sort` is `newest`,
`name` or `attribute:<key>`; `direction` is `asc` or `desc`; `cursor` is the opaque token
a previous page returned. Nothing here is validated against a schema — that is the use
case's job, the only place that can read one.

PartSearchResponse.title: PartSearchResponse
PartSearchResponse.description:
One page of results and the cursor the next one continues from (requirement 4.11).

The cursor is the opaque token `SearchCursor.encode` builds, `None` on the last page; a
client sends it back untouched as `PartSearchRequest.cursor` (requirement 4.3).

PartStockResponse.title: PartStockResponse
PartStockResponse.description:
A part's total on_hand and its breakdown by location (requirements 7.3, 7.4).

A part never received reports a total of zero and an empty breakdown, not a 404.

PartSummaryResponse.title: PartSummaryResponse
PartSummaryResponse.description:
A part as the list shows it: no attribute values, because a page of rows must not
resolve one schema per row (requirement 8.2).

PartTotalResponse.title: PartTotalResponse
PartTotalResponse.description: One part's total on_hand, for the batch the parts list asks for (requirements 7.1, 7.2).

PinRequest.title: PinRequest
PinRequest.description:
One row of a pin table, every cell as the owner typed or pasted it.

Nothing here is checked beyond being text, on purpose, `type` included: the domain is
the one authority on what a pin number or a voltage is, and it is the only thing that
can say which row and which cell a refusal is about (requirement 3.1). A `Literal` on
`type` would answer a pasted `GPIO` with a validation error naming neither.

PinResponse.title: PinResponse
PinResponse.description:
One stored pin. `number` comes back upper-cased and `voltage` in volts, whatever
was typed: normalizing is the domain's, and this is what it kept (requirements 2.1, 2.9).

PinoutResponse.title: PinoutResponse
PinoutResponse.description: A part's pins in their saved order; `[]` for a part with none, never a 404 (1.2).

PlannedUnitResponse.title: PlannedUnitResponse
PlannedUnitResponse.description:
One unit a row will receive: its serial and MAC in their canonical forms, both null
for an unlabelled unit.

ProjectResponse.title: ProjectResponse
ProjectResponse.description:
A project page (requirement 1.6): its revisions oldest first, the one it opens on, and
the label a new revision would take, which the fork dialog prefills. `next_label` is null
only when no label can be suggested within 16 characters.

ProjectSummaryResponse.title: ProjectSummaryResponse
ProjectSummaryResponse.description: A row of the project list (requirement 3.1).

ProjectTagResponse.title: ProjectTagResponse
ProjectTagResponse.description: A tag of the workspace and how many projects carry it (requirement 2.6).

QuickAddRequest.title: QuickAddRequest
QuickAddRequest.description:
A part, optionally its first stock, and for a duplicate the part whose pinout it
copies (requirements 1 and 3.2).

QuickAddResponse.title: QuickAddResponse
QuickAddResponse.description:
What a quick-add added: the part, and the lot's balance or the units it received, each
with its minted code and location (requirements 1.2, 1.3). `balance` is null for units
and for a part added without stock.

QuickPartBody.title: QuickPartBody
QuickPartBody.description:
The part half of a quick-add, as the dialog typed it (requirement 1.1).

Every field may be left out, the category and the name too: the catalog is the one
authority on what a new part needs, so a blank one comes back as a `missing` problem on
its field, beside every other problem, rather than as a schema refusal on its own (1.5).
Attribute values are what the part form sends, text as typed (`4k7`) or a switch's
boolean; null or blank text is nothing given.

QuickStockBody.title: QuickStockBody
QuickStockBody.description:
Where a quick-add's first stock goes and how much (design decision 11).

Both halves or no stock at all: a body giving one without the other is refused by the
schema, naming the one it lacks (requirement 1.7). The quantity's range is left to the use
case, since it depends on how the part is counted, and is reported with every other
problem (1.8).

RangeFilterRequest.title: RangeFilterRequest
RangeFilterRequest.description:
A number range on an attribute: a minimum, a maximum, or both, as the owner typed them.

The bounds stay text (`1k`, `4k7`) until the category's schema reads them with the
attribute's unit — the same reason a part's values arrive as text (requirement 2.2).

ReceiveRequest.title: ReceiveRequest
ReceiveRequest.description: Receiving a positive quantity of a part into a location (requirement 4.1).

ReceiveUnitsRequest.title: ReceiveUnitsRequest
ReceiveUnitsRequest.description:
Receiving units of a unit-tracked part into a location (requirement 1.1).

The `units` list's length is the quantity: one entry per unit, so N units are one
`RECEIVE` of N on the (part, location) lot. At least one unit, since a receipt of nothing
is nothing to do, and at most the web form's hundred: each unit mints its code with its
own statement, so an unbounded list would hold the transaction open for as long as it
was long.

ReceiveUnitsResponse.title: ReceiveUnitsResponse
ReceiveUnitsResponse.description:
A receipt's result: the units created (each with its minted code) and the lot's new
balance, so the web shows the codes and updates the balance without a refetch (design's
HTTP API).

RelabelUnitRequest.title: RelabelUnitRequest
RelabelUnitRequest.description:
A unit's serial and MAC, both optional and both replaced by what the body carries.

A field left `null` clears that label; the use case refuses a duplicate and commits
nothing when neither changed (requirement 5.6).

ReplacePinoutRequest.title: ReplacePinoutRequest
ReplacePinoutRequest.description:
The part's whole pinout, because a pinout is replaced and never patched (design §2).

No pins at all is a table cleared, not a body left out, so the field has a default and
`{"pins": []}` and `{}` mean the same thing (requirement 1.4).

RetireUnitRequest.title: RetireUnitRequest
RetireUnitRequest.description: Retiring a unit, with the reason it left stock; `damaged` when the body omits it (3.1).

RevisionResponse.title: RevisionResponse
RevisionResponse.description: A revision on the wire: `A - breadboard` is the label `A` and the summary.

RevisionSummaryResponse.title: RevisionSummaryResponse
RevisionSummaryResponse.description: The latest revision as a list row shows it: `B - perfboard`, with its status.

SchemaAttributeResponse.title: SchemaAttributeResponse
SchemaAttributeResponse.description: A field of a resolved schema, marked when it comes from a category above this one.

SearchResultResponse.title: SearchResultResponse
SearchResultResponse.description:
A part as the results table shows it: the summary, plus the values of the category's
number and enum attributes, for the columns the web adds when a category is chosen
(requirement 6.3). Empty when no category was searched, since there is no schema then.

SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse
SessionResponse.description: A logged-in device. `current` marks the one making this request.

ShortageReportResponse.title: ShortageReportResponse
ShortageReportResponse.description: The summary, and each part in the order it first appears on the BOM.

ShortageSummaryResponse.title: ShortageSummaryResponse
ShortageSummaryResponse.description: The report's counts, and whether the BOM is complete (requirement 6.6).

StockOutcomeResponse.title: StockOutcomeResponse
StockOutcomeResponse.description:
What a row puts away, and where (requirement 7.2): a lot's quantity, or units, whose
count is the quantity and each of which is listed with its labels.

TextFilterRequest.title: TextFilterRequest
TextFilterRequest.description: A fragment a text attribute has to contain, ignoring case (requirement 2.5).

UnitResponse.title: UnitResponse
UnitResponse.description:
A unit on the wire: its identity, its status, and where it sits (requirements 6.1, 8.3).

The location is the unit's lot's location, resolved by the API; it is present for every
unit (a unit always points at a lot in some location), but typed optional so a response
never fails to serialize if a lot were ever missing. The MAC and serial are the canonical
stored forms.

UpdateAttributeRequest.title: UpdateAttributeRequest
UpdateAttributeRequest.description: Label, required, options and position. `key` and `kind` are refused (requirement 2.9).

UpdateCategoryRequest.title: UpdateCategoryRequest
UpdateCategoryRequest.description:
A rename, a move, a flag change, or a mix. What the body left out is left alone.

`parent_id: null` is a move to the root, which is a different thing from not sending
it, so the handler asks `moves()` rather than reading the value. `tracked_individually`
and `not_stocked` are tri-state the same way: `null` clears the flag back to inheriting,
`true`/`false` overrides, and leaving it out changes nothing — so the handler asks
`sets_tracking()` and `sets_stocking()`.

UpdateLocationRequest.title: UpdateLocationRequest
UpdateLocationRequest.description:
A rename, a move, or both. What the body left out is left alone.

`parent_id: null` is a move to the root, a different thing from not sending it, so the
handler asks `moves()` rather than reading the value, as catalog's category patch does.

UpdatePartRequest.title: UpdatePartRequest
UpdatePartRequest.description:
Replaces the details and the whole attribute map (requirement 4.8).

`category_id` left out keeps the part where it is; sent, it moves the part and the
values are validated against the new category's schema (requirement 4.10).

UpdateProjectRequest.title: UpdateProjectRequest
UpdateProjectRequest.description: A project's name, description and tags, replacing the stored ones whole (1.5).

UpdateRevisionRequest.title: UpdateRevisionRequest
UpdateRevisionRequest.description: A revision's label, summary and notes, replacing the stored ones whole (4.8).

VoltageResponse.title: VoltageResponse
VoltageResponse.description:
A pin's stored level in the two forms requirement 2.13 asks for.

A string and not a JSON number, for the reason `AttributeValueResponse.value` is one:
JSON numbers are doubles in every client we generate, and the level is exact.
